dhp100:1: Though a speech consist of a thousand words, if the sentences lack meaning,
dhp100:3: Better were a single sentence full of meaning, which if a man hear, he is at peace.
dhp101:1: Though a Stanza consist of a thousand words, if the sentences lack meaning,
dhp101:3: Better were a single sentence of a Stanza, which if a man hear he is at peace.
dhp102:1: Though one should recite a hundred Stanzas composed of meaningless sentences,
dhp102:3: Yet one Sentence of the Law were better, which if a man hear he is at peace.
dhp103:1: Though one should conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle,
dhp103:3: Yet would he be the mightiest conqueror who should conquer one, himself.
dhp104:1: Victory over self is better than victory over all other folk besides;
dhp104:3: If a man conquer self, and live always under restraint,
dhp105:1: Neither god nor gandhabba nor Māra with Brahmā united,
dhp105:3: Can turn into defeat the victory of such a man.
dhp106:1: Though a man, month after month, for a hundred years, should sacrifice a thousand pieces of money,
dhp106:3: Yet, should he honor for even a single instant a man who has trained himself,
dhp106:5: It were better for him so to render honor than to offer sacrifice for a hundred years.
dhp107:1: Though a man for a hundred years should tend the sacrificial fire in the forest,
dhp107:3: Yet, should he honor for even a single instant a man who has trained himself,
dhp107:5: It were better for him so to render honor than to offer sacrifice for a hundred years.
dhp108:1: Whatsoever, either by way of sacrificial slaughter or by way of oblation,
dhp108:2: Though it be for a year, a man sacrifice, desiring merit,
dhp108:3: All that comes not to the value of a fourth part;
dhp108:4: If a man have the habit of reverence.
dhp109:1: If a man have the habit of reverence, if he alway respect the aged.
dhp109:3: Four things increase for him: age, beauty, happiness, power.
dhp110:1: Though one should live a hundred years, corrupt, not meditating,
dhp110:3: Yet were it better to live a single day in the practice of virtue, in meditation.
dhp111:1: Though one should live a hundred years, unwise, not meditating,
dhp111:3: Yet were it better to live a single day possessed of wisdom, in meditation.
dhp112:1: Though one should live a hundred years, idle, listless,
dhp112:3: Yet were it better to live for a single day, and strive with might and main.
dhp113:1: Though one should live a hundred years, ‘twere all in vain,
dhp113:2: Did one not see that all that is doth wax and wane;
dhp113:3: Instead, ‘twere better far to live a single day,
dhp113:4: And know that all the world contains doth rise and pass away.
dhp114:1: Though one should live a hundred years, the region of the deathless never seeing,
dhp114:2: ’Twould be in vain; instead, ‘twould better be
dhp114:3: To live a single day, the region of the deathless seeing.
dhp115:1: Though one should live a hundred years, did he not behold the Law Supreme,
dhp115:3: It were better that he live but a single day and behold the Law Supreme.
